drafts.text:
ChatGPT's dot now takes texts. Hand it a task or something to watch, by text, photo or voice note, and it texts you back when there's news.

The biggest AI launch of the week is basically 'the agent messages you first.'

That's the part most of us skip when we build agents. We build the chat. We forget the nudge.

In Copilot Studio, start with the trigger, not the topic.
drafts.video_tip: Vertical 20s: phone on the desk buzzes with an agent update, cut to Copilot Studio showing an autonomous trigger being added. Caption: 'Stop waiting for users to ask.'

drafts.text:
If you're on ChatGPT Pro or Business, check whether you're eligible: OpenAI is handing out up to $500 a month in API credits to build apps and agents.

That's not a perk. That's a sandbox budget.

The agent idea you've been pitching in meetings for six months? Build the ugly version this weekend and bring a demo instead of a slide.
drafts.video_tip: Talking head 15s holding a sticky note that says '$500/mo', then slap it onto a whiteboard labelled 'agent backlog'. End card: 'Demo > deck.'

drafts.text:
Microsoft's quarter in three numbers: $92.3 billion revenue, $63.9 billion Microsoft Cloud, 48% Azure growth.

Satya's framing on the call: building the new tech stack for the agentic wave.

If you work in Power Platform or Copilot Studio, read that as a career signal, not a stock tip.

The budget is moving to agents. Be the person in your org who can actually ship one.
drafts.video_tip: Carousel or 20s motion graphic: three big numbers stacked ($92.3B, $63.9B, 48%), then a final slide with a Copilot Studio canvas and the line 'Your move.'

drafts.text:
GitHub's Octoverse numbers for the last year: 17.9 billion pushes, 34.3 billion commits, 1.3 billion merged pull requests.

Same week, Burke Holland is calling Copilot Projects 'an agent to manage your agents', local or cloud.

We've officially reached middle management for bots.

My only question: who runs the 1:1s?
